name: ieee80211_rx_mgmt_beacon
prose: Static function ieee80211_rx_mgmt_beacon(link, hdr, len, rx_status) handling a received beacon (normal or S1G) on a managed link; the wiphy lock is held (asserted) and the function returns nothing. It returns with no state change if the variable part starts beyond len, if there is no channel context, or if ieee80211_rx_beacon_freq_valid fails. If an association is pending (assoc_data with need_beacon) and the beacon is from that BSS, it parses the elements (returning if that fails), calls ieee80211_rx_bss_info, records DTIM period, have_beacon, timing data, MBSSID periodicity and EMA support, restarts the association timeout (run_again), frees the elements and returns. Otherwise it returns unless the interface is associated and the beacon is from the associated BSS. For an associated beacon it first processes signal-strength handling (unless the signal is unavailable), cancels a pending AP probe and resets the beacon-loss monitor; these happen before the elements are parsed, so state changes even if parsing then fails. It parses the elements with the care_about_ies filter and returns if that fails; a decrypted beacon with an SSID mismatch disconnects and returns (the code returns there without freeing elems). It then handles TIM-based null-function / PS-poll sending, P2P NoA updates, timing sync, and skips the rest when the beacon CRC is unchanged (or for an S1G short beacon). Otherwise it stores the CRC, calls ieee80211_rx_bss_info and ieee80211_sta_process_chanswitch (beacon source), sets the DTIM period on the first beacon, updates the BSS parameter change count and ERP/capability info, and, if the non-transmitted MBSSID profile is missing, jumps to apply. It also processes cross-link CSA, WMM parameters, TWT, bandwidth (a failing ieee80211_config_bw disconnects the station and frees the elements without applying changes), operating mode notification, power constraint, ML reconfiguration and TTLM. At apply it notifies the driver of the accumulated changes with ieee80211_link_info_change_notify, and at free it frees the parsed elements.
note: Reviewer 15 right: the parse failure occurs after the signal handling, probe cancel and beacon-monitor reset (mlme.c:7494-7522), so state changes. Also found: the SSID-mismatch return at 7536 skips kfree(elems). Slice cut the head (function at 7386).

name: ieee80211_mgd_assoc
prose: Function ieee80211_mgd_assoc(sdata, req) starting an association; it returns 0 or a negative errno. It first returns -EOPNOTSUPP for a 4-address MLO request, then allocates a temporary assoc_data (-ENOMEM on failure) and returns -EINVAL if the AP is in a CSA process or the BSS has no SSID element (or one that is too long). It copies the SSID and AP address, and if the interface is associated it disassociates first. It copies the HT/VHT/S1G capability settings from the request, and for an MLO request (ap_mld_addr set) returns -EINVAL if HT/VHT/HE/EHT is disabled in the flags, or for any link BSS without WMM, on S1GHz, whose connection mode is below EHT, or whose HT/VHT capability setup fails (setting req->links[i].error); for a non-MLO request it returns -EINVAL if 6 GHz is combined with disabled HT/VHT/HE and returns the error of ieee80211_mgd_get_ap_ht_vht_capa. It returns -EBUSY if authentication is not yet done or another association is already pending (ifmgd->assoc_data non-NULL, which is left untouched); a non-matching auth_data is destroyed first. A FILS KEK longer than FILS_MAX_KEK_LEN gives -EINVAL. It then sets up links (ieee80211_vif_set_links for MLO), the connection settings, U-APSD, MFP, RRM and control-port settings, and installs assoc_data as ifmgd->assoc_data. Later failures (other links' ieee80211_prep_channel, ieee80211_prep_connection, or the missing-link WARN) go to err_clear, which, if there is no auth_data, zeroes the deflink BSSID and notifies BSS_CHANGED_BSSID, then sets ifmgd->assoc_data to NULL and frees the temporary assoc_data; failures before the install free only the temporary assoc_data and leave ifmgd->assoc_data as it was. On success it may set need_beacon (NEED_DTIM_BEFORE_ASSOC with no beacon IEs), calls run_again, destroys the auth_data and returns 0.
note: Reviewer 15 right: the -EBUSY return when ifmgd->assoc_data already exists leaves it non-NULL (mlme.c:9884-9887, err_free skips the NULL assignment at 10052); the old text said every failure leaves it NULL. Slice cut the head (function at 9665).

name: _ieee802_11_parse_elems_full
prose: Static function _ieee802_11_parse_elems_full(params, elems_parse, check_inherit) in net/mac80211/parse.c (the packet name ieee802_11_parse_elems_crc is not in the file) which parses an information-element buffer into elems_parse->elems and returns the CRC. The CRC starts at params->crc; if params->filter is non-zero, each element with id below 64 whose bit is set in the filter updates it with crc32_be over the whole element (header included), and extension elements are passed a pointer to the CRC so ieee80211_parse_extension_element can update it; with a zero filter the CRC is returned unchanged. It iterates the elements of params->start / params->len. If check_inherit is given, elements not inherited (cfg80211_is_element_inherited) are skipped. For a set of ids (SSID, rates, TIM, RSN, HT/VHT operation, mesh and channel-switch elements, S1G elements and others) a second occurrence sets IEEE80211_PARSE_ERR_DUP_ELEM in elems->parse_error and is skipped. For each known element applicable to params->mode (and params->action for action frames) it stores a pointer into the input buffer (and length where needed) in the elems fields, or ORs the matching IEEE80211_PARSE_ERR_* (for example BAD_ELEM_SIZE or UNEXPECTED_ELEM) into elems->parse_error; an element that parsed without error is marked seen. After the loop, if the buffer did not end on an element boundary it ORs IEEE80211_PARSE_ERR_INVALID_END into parse_error. It allocates nothing and takes no lock.
note: The old text said the CRC is only updated over the Cisco DTPC element and extension elements; in the code every filtered element with id < 64 contributes (parse.c:358-361), and the Cisco DTPC element has no special CRC handling. The function is _ieee802_11_parse_elems_full (parse.c:283-745).

name: ieee80211_rx_h_defragment
prose: Static rx handler ieee80211_rx_h_defragment(rx) (name was ieee80211_rx_h_defrag in the packet) reassembling fragmented MPDUs; it returns an rx result. It returns RX_CONTINUE for control and extension frames. A non-fragment (no more-fragments bit and fragment number 0) goes straight to the exit: it updates the RX LED and, when rx->sta is set, increments the link station's rx packet counter, and returns RX_CONTINUE. A fragmented frame with a multicast address returns RX_DROP_U_MCAST_FRAGMENT; a failing skb_linearize returns RX_DROP_U_OOM. For fragment number 0 it adds a new entry with ieee80211_reassemble_add (taking the skb), records for CCMP/GCMP protected frames the PN, protected state and key colour (or only protected state and key colour for other protected frames) and returns RX_QUEUED. For later fragments it looks the entry up (RX_DROP_U_DEFRAG_MISMATCH if none), checks protection: for an entry that requires sequential PNs it returns RX_DROP_U_NONSEQ_PN if the current frame does not need it, RX_DROP_U_BAD_KEY_COLOR on a key colour mismatch, RX_DROP_U_REPLAY if the PN is not the previous plus one; for other protected entries it returns RX_DROP_U_EXPECT_DEFRAG_PROT if the frame or key does not match, or RX_DROP_U_BAD_KEY_COLOR for a colour mismatch on a decrypted frame. It then pulls the header; if the accumulated length would exceed U16_MAX it purges the entry's queue and returns RX_DROP_U_DEFRAG_OVERFLOW. It appends the fragment; if more fragments follow it sets rx->skb to NULL and returns RX_QUEUED. For the last fragment it takes the first queued skb as rx->skb, expands its head if tailroom is short (RX_DROP_U_OOM after purging if that fails), appends and frees the other fragments, and then takes the common exit and returns RX_CONTINUE.
note: Name in the packet was wrong (function is ieee80211_rx_h_defragment, rx.c:2269); the old prose's return list is largely right but did not mention the RX_CONTINUE exit for non-fragments and control frames, the multicast and linearize drops, or the first-fragment RX_QUEUED path.

name: sta_set_sinfo
prose: Function sta_set_sinfo(sta, sinfo, tidstats) filling a station_info; the packet slice held only part of it, and the function starts at sta_info.c:2984. It sets sinfo->generation, copies the beacon count for a station-type vif into rx_beacon, then calls drv_sta_statistics so the driver may fill fields first. After that it unconditionally sets the filled bits for INACTIVE_TIME, STA_FLAGS, BSS_PARAM, CONNECTED_TIME, ASSOC_AT_BOOTTIME and RX_DROP_MISC and overwrites connected_time, assoc_at and inactive_time (the driver's values for those are replaced), and also sets beacon_loss_count (with its filled bit) for a station vif. For tx bytes/packets, rx bytes/packets, tx retries/failed, rx/tx duration, airtime weight, signal, signal average, chain signals, tx/rx bitrate, ack signal and average ack signal it fills the field from mac80211's own statistics only if the driver did not already mark that field filled (rx bytes and the duration fields are accumulated with +=), and sets the filled bit. rx_dropped_misc is always recomputed from the station and per-CPU counters, the BSS parameter block (CTS protection, short preamble, short slot, DTIM period, beacon interval) and the station flags set and mask are always written, without a driver-filled check; per-TID statistics are filled only when tidstats is true and cfg80211_sinfo_alloc_tid_stats succeeds (the caller then owns the allocated array); mesh vifs get mesh info; expected_throughput is filled when non-zero. For an MLD station it copies the MLD address, sets valid_links, and fills each link with sta_set_link_sinfo, clearing from valid_links any link whose link_sta, link or sinfo->links entry is missing. It returns nothing.
note: Reviewer 15 partly right: rx_dropped_misc, bss_param and sta_flags are always overwritten (sta_info.c:3098-3151) regardless of what the driver filled, but their filled bits are set before the writes (3003-3008), not omitted; and connected_time, assoc_at and inactive_time are also unconditionally overwritten. The old text claimed fields the driver filled are left untouched, which is false for those.

name: ieee80211_reconfig
prose: Function ieee80211_reconfig(local) reconfiguring the driver after a hardware restart or resume; the wiphy lock is held (asserted) and it returns 0 or a negative errno. If local->open_count is 0 it skips the reprogramming and goes to the wake_up part. With CONFIG_PM and local->suspended it sets local->resuming; if local->wowlan is set it clears suspended, calls drv_resume and clears wowlan: a negative result clears resuming and is returned; a result of 0 goes to wake_up (no full reconfiguration); a result of 1 means a regular reset was requested, so suspended is restored and reconfiguration proceeds. Without wowlan no drv_resume call is made and reconfiguration always proceeds. Reconfiguration: drv_start (on failure it warns, wakes the queues by suspend reason, calls ieee80211_handle_reconfig_failure and returns the error); fragmentation and RTS thresholds, coverage class; adding the monitor and running interfaces with drv_add_interface (on failure, already added interfaces are removed, ieee80211_handle_reconfig_failure is called and the error returned); channel contexts; hw config and filters; per-interface BSS information, links and stations; null-function frames; AP stations; keys; multi-link active links; and restarting a scheduled scan (reporting it as stopped if it cannot be rescheduled). wake_up (reached also from the early exits): with AMPDU aggregation it tears down BA sessions (unless resuming) and clears WLAN_STA_BLOCK_BA; drv_reconfig_complete (restart type) is called for an open device when not suspended or after a wowlan-triggered reset; if local->in_reconfig it clears it, re-schedules remain-on-channel and sdata work; the suspend-reason queue stop is released; for in_reconfig it restarts station interfaces; the virtual monitor is added if needed. If the device was not suspended it returns 0; otherwise it clears suspended then resuming, flushes a completed scan, calls drv_reconfig_complete (suspend type) unless wowlan reset, restarts station interfaces, arms the station cleanup timer and returns 0.
note: Reviewer 15 partly wrong: after a successful drv_resume (result 0) under wowlan the code does goto wake_up (util.c:1787-1788), skipping full reconfiguration; the old prose was right for that case but did not say it applies only with local->wowlan. The old claim that open_count == 0 returns immediately was also imprecise: it jumps to wake_up (1766-1767) which still runs the wake-up steps. Slice cut the head (function at 1749).

name: mac802154_llsec_decrypt
prose: Function mac802154_llsec_decrypt(sec, skb) verifying and decrypting an 802.15.4 frame (the packet name ieee802154_llsec_decrypt does not exist; the slice held only its start). It returns -EINVAL if ieee802154_hdr_peek fails, 0 if the security-enabled bit is clear, and -EINVAL if the frame version is 0 or sec->params.enabled is false (read under sec->lock, which is released at once). These early returns happen before the RCU lock or any key is taken. It then takes rcu_read_lock and looks up the key (-ENOKEY if none, with a key reference taken otherwise), the device by source address (-EINVAL if none), and the security level entry for the frame type (-EINVAL if the lookup fails). It returns -EINVAL if hdr.sec.level is not in seclevel.sec_levels while the level is 0, device_override is set and the device is not seclevel_exempt, -EOVERFLOW if the frame counter is 0xffffffff, and the error of llsec_update_devkey_info if that fails (for example -ENOENT or -EINVAL for a bad counter). On these failures it drops the key reference with llsec_key_put and releases the RCU lock, and skb is not modified. On success it copies the device address, releases the RCU lock, calls llsec_do_decrypt(skb, sec, &hdr, key, dev_addr), drops the key reference and returns that call's result.
note: Name was a placeholder; the function is mac802154_llsec_decrypt (llsec.c:1005-1066). Old prose said the read lock, RCU lock and key reference are released on every path; the early returns precede them. Also the lookup order is key first, then device, then seclevel.

name: ipgre_tunnel_encap_del_mpls_ops
prose: Static function ipgre_tunnel_encap_del_mpls_ops(void) in net/mpls/af_mpls.c; with CONFIG_NET_IP_TUNNEL it calls ip_tunnel_encap_del_ops(&mpls_iptun_ops, TUNNEL_ENCAP_MPLS) and ignores the result, otherwise it is an empty function. ip_tunnel_encap_del_ops returns -ERANGE for an out-of-range slot number; otherwise it atomically clears the TUNNEL_ENCAP_MPLS slot only if it still holds mpls_iptun_ops (cmpxchg; result 0, or -1 when it held something else, in which case the slot is not changed) and then always calls synchronize_net(), so the function may sleep and must be called from process context outside an RCU read-side section. It returns nothing.
note: Reviewer 15 half right: the slot is cleared only if it still holds mpls_iptun_ops (ip_tunnel.c:479-481), but synchronize_net() runs regardless of the cmpxchg result, not only on success (483); reviewer 2 right on synchronize_net always running but wrong that the slot is cleared unconditionally; reviewer 1 right that it may sleep. Slice shows the wrapper at af_mpls.c:59-62.

name: mptcp_pm_add_timer
prose: Static function mptcp_pm_add_timer(timer), the ADD_ADDR retransmission timer handler (timer is the add_timer of a struct mptcp_pm_add_addr entry whose sock holds a reference taken when the timer was armed); it returns nothing. It takes bh_lock_sock on the MPTCP socket and always releases it and drops the timer's socket reference with sock_put before returning (it takes no new reference). The timeout starts at 0. If the socket state is TCP_CLOSE it leaves with timeout 0; if the socket is owned by user space it leaves with timeout HZ/20; otherwise it gets timeout = mptcp_adjust_add_addr_timeout(msk) and leaves with that timeout without retransmitting if it is zero or an ADD_ADDR signal is already pending. Otherwise, under msk->pm.lock, if entry->retrans_times is below ADD_ADDR_RETRANS_MAX and no ADD_ADDR signal is pending, it announces the address again, sends the ADD_ADDR ack and increments retrans_times. Then if retrans_times is still below the maximum the timeout is shifted left by retrans_times, else the timeout becomes 0; after unlocking pm.lock, in the latter case it calls mptcp_pm_subflow_established(msk). At the exit, a non-zero timeout re-arms the timer with sk_reset_timer at jiffies plus the timeout; a zero timeout sets entry->timer_done to true instead.
note: Prose matches pm.c:341-400; reviewers' points (reschedule when socket owned, early exits, subflow_established, only releases a reference) are all already reflected in the packet text.

name: mptcp_win_from_space
prose: Static inline function mptcp_win_from_space(sk, space) for an MPTCP socket: it returns __tcp_win_from_space(mptcp_sk(sk)->scaling_ratio, space), i.e. the int truncation of ((s64)space * scaling_ratio) >> TCP_RMEM_TO_WIN_SCALE. No clamping is done: for a negative space the result is negative (arithmetic right shift of a negative value), for zero it is 0. It takes no lock or reference and allocates nothing.
note: Reviewer 15 right: the code does not clamp (protocol.h:401-404; tcp.h:1639-1644), so negative space yields a negative result; reviewers 1 right that space may be negative and 2 wrong that __tcp_win_from_space clamps. Contract left empty (depends on the socket's scaling_ratio field).

name: ncsi_aen_handler_lsc
prose: Static function ncsi_aen_handler_lsc(ndp, h) handling a link-status-change AEN packet. It finds the channel for h->common.channel and returns -ENODEV, changing nothing, if there is none. Otherwise, under the channel lock it stores the packet's status in modes[NCSI_MODE_LINK].data[2] and oem_status in data[4], notes whether the link was up before and after (bit 0 of data[2]), and whether the channel is already chained on a queue and its state; it logs a warning if the channel is inactive. It returns 0 with no further action if the link state did not change or the channel is already chained. If the device has neither multi-package nor a multi-channel package: a link going down sets NCSI_DEV_RESHUFFLE, stops the channel monitor, queues the channel on ndp->channel_queue and returns the result of ncsi_process_next_channel(ndp); a link coming up returns 0. Otherwise (multi-channel): if the link went down, then if the channel is the last one it returns the result of ncsi_reset_dev(&ndp->ndev), else if Tx is enabled on it it calls ncsi_update_tx_channel to fail over (result ignored); if the link came up it moves Tx back to the preferred channel, or to this channel when the current Tx channel has no link; all those multi-channel cases other than the reset return 0.
note: Prose matches ncsi-aen.c:46-138; the reviewers' points (-ENODEV, failover via ncsi_update_tx_channel returns 0) are right and already in the packet text; added the unchanged-link and chained-channel early return.

name: ip_set_dump_do
prose: Static function ip_set_dump_do(skb, cb) producing one netlink dump message for ip_set; the slice cut the head (function at ip_set_core.c:1578). It returns -EINVAL if cb->args[IPSET_CB_DUMP] is 0. If cb->args[IPSET_CB_INDEX] is already >= ip_set_max it jumps to out and returns skb->len. It derives dump_type and dump_flags from args[IPSET_CB_DUMP] and loops over set indexes from args[IPSET_CB_INDEX] (the loop increment advances the stored index on every pass). For each index it takes ip_set_ref_lock for writing: a missing set or a destroyed instance returns -ENOENT for DUMP_ONE, returns 0 (to out) if the instance is being destroyed, and otherwise skips to the next index; sets not matching the current pass (DUMP_ALL versus DUMP_LAST by IPSET_DUMP_LAST) are skipped (index advanced by the loop). For a selected set, if args[IPSET_CB_ARG0] is 0 it takes a netlink reference (ref_netlink++); it then starts a message with start_msg (-EMSGSIZE if that fails, going to release_refcount) and puts the protocol and set name; failure to put them gives -EFAULT. For IPSET_FLAG_LIST_SETNAME it finishes the set (next_set). For ARG0 == 0 it also emits the type, family, revision (and index for newer protocols) and calls set->variant->head (an error is returned via release_refcount); with IPSET_FLAG_LIST_HEADER it finishes the set; otherwise it calls variant->uref and then variant->list; if list returns with ARG0 zero the set is done (next_set), else it goes to release_refcount without advancing the index. next_set sets the index to IPSET_INVALID_ID for DUMP_ONE and otherwise increments it. release_refcount runs only if ret is non-zero or ARG0 is zero: it finds the set, calls variant->uref(false), drops the netlink reference and resets ARG0 to 0; with ret 0 and ARG0 non-zero the reference and ARG0 are kept for the next call. After a completed DUMP_ALL pass the function switches args[IPSET_CB_DUMP] to DUMP_LAST (flags preserved), resets the index to 0 and runs the loop again. At out, if a message was started it is ended with nlmsg_end, and the function returns ret if negative, else skb->len. One message is started per call at most, because each started message leads to out; ip_set_ref_lock is not held on return.
note: Reviewer 1 right (reference kept when list returns with ARG0 nonzero), reviewer 2 right (index not advanced on partial listing or error paths), reviewer 15 right that the for-loop increment also advances the index on the continue paths (ip_set_core.c:1602, 1618, 1627); its claim that earlier messages are never ended does not apply because only one message is started per call.

name: IPSET_TOKEN(HTYPE, _create)(struct net *net, struct ip_set *set, struct nlattr *tb[], u32 flags)
prose: Generated static function IPSET_TOKEN(HTYPE, _create)(net, set, tb, flags) in ip_set_hash_gen.h, the create handler of a hash set type (emitted with IP_SET_EMIT_CREATE); the slice cut its head (function at 1472). flags is not used. It returns -IPSET_ERR_INVALID_FAMILY if set->family is not IPv4 or IPv6 (or, for IP_SET_PROTO_UNDEF types, is not NFPROTO_UNSPEC), -IPSET_ERR_PROTOCOL if the optional HASHSIZE, MAXELEM, TIMEOUT or CADT_FLAGS attributes are not in network byte order, and for types with a mark mask, netmask or bitmask returns -IPSET_ERR_INVALID_MARKMASK, -IPSET_ERR_INVALID_NETMASK or -IPSET_ERR_BITMASK_NETMASK_EXCL for invalid or conflicting values. It reads IPSET_ATTR_HASHSIZE (raised to IPSET_MIMINAL_HASHSIZE if smaller) and IPSET_ATTR_MAXELEM; it does not reject too large values. It allocates the hash header and the table (hash bits are fls(hashsize - 1)), returning -ENOMEM if the header, the table size computation, the table or the region array fails, freeing what was allocated. It then sets maxelem, the bit/net masks, the initval (from IPSET_ATTR_INITVAL or random), the bucket size (clamped, rounded up to even), htable_bits, the per-region maxelem, publishes the table with RCU_INIT_POINTER, sets set->data, set->variant and set->dsize for the IPv4 or IPv6 variant and set->timeout (IPSET_NO_TIMEOUT unless IPSET_ATTR_TIMEOUT is given, in which case the garbage collector is initialised), and returns 0.
note: Reviewer 15 right: the code reads IPSET_ATTR_HASHSIZE (not HTABLE_SIZE). The old text also listed -IPSET_ERR_EXIST, -IPSET_ERR_HASH_SIZE and -IPSET_ERR_MAXELEM, which this function never returns, and omitted the family, protocol and mask errors. Name changed to the full macro-generated head.

name: hash_netportnet6_uadt
prose: Static function hash_netportnet6_uadt(set, tb, adt, lineno, flags, retried), the IPv6 add/delete/test handler of the hash:net,port,net set type (the packet name hash_netportnet_uadt does not exist; the slice held only its tail). It stores the line number if given, and returns -IPSET_ERR_PROTOCOL if the IP, IP2 or PORT attribute is missing or PORT, PORT_TO or CADT_FLAGS are not in network order, -IPSET_ERR_HASH_RANGE_UNSUPPORTED if IP_TO or IP2_TO is given, the error of ip_set_get_ipaddr6 for either address, and the error of ip_set_get_extensions. It returns -IPSET_ERR_INVALID_CIDR if CIDR or CIDR2 exceeds HOST_MASK, applies the masks to both addresses, reads the port, returns -IPSET_ERR_MISSING_PROTO if PROTO is absent and -IPSET_ERR_INVALID_PROTO if it is 0; the port is zeroed unless the protocol uses ports (or is ICMPv6); an IPSET_FLAG_NOMATCH in CADT_FLAGS is copied into flags. For IPSET_TEST, for protocols without ports, or when PORT_TO is absent, it calls adtfn once and returns -ret if ip_set_enomatch(ret, flags, adt, set) holds, 0 if ip_set_eexist(ret, flags) holds, and ret otherwise. Otherwise it takes the port range [PORT, PORT_TO] (swapped if reversed, starting from h->next.port when retried) and calls adtfn for each port, returning the first error that is not an ignorable exist error, or 0 when all succeed.
note: Name was wrong: the slice is the end of hash_netportnet6_uadt (ip_set_hash_netportnet.c:473-612); the IPv4 variant is hash_netportnet4_uadt at 188. The old prose omitted the missing-attribute, range-unsupported and address-parse errors and gave the NOMATCH/EXIST return rule loosely (ip_set_enomatch decides, not 'NOMATCH set and ret nonzero').

name: todrop_entry
prose: Static inline function todrop_entry(cp) deciding whether to drop a connection entry (random drop under memory pressure); it uses the function-static arrays todrop_rate (0 to 8) and todrop_counter without any locking, so the callers must not run it concurrently (the comment says it is called from timer bottom-half context; its caller ip_vs_random_dropentry also runs it from process context). It returns 0 if time_before(cp->timeout + jiffies, cp->timer.expires + 60*HZ) (the connection has not lasted 60 seconds), if the incoming packet count in_pkts is outside [0, 8], or if todrop_rate[in_pkts] is 0. Otherwise it decrements todrop_counter[in_pkts]; if the result is still greater than 0 it returns 0 (the counter stays decremented); otherwise it resets todrop_counter[in_pkts] to todrop_rate[in_pkts] and returns 1.
note: All three reviewers right: the 60-second check comes first and returns 0 (ip_vs_conn.c:1270-1271); the counter is decremented on the return-0 path at 1279; and the 'called only from timer softirq' claim cannot be relied on (it is the comment in the code, and the caller ip_vs_random_dropentry runs elsewhere). The statement is now qualified.

name: ip_vs_conn_drop_conntrack
prose: Function ip_vs_conn_drop_conntrack(cp) trying to delete the connection-tracking entry of an IPVS connection; it returns nothing. It returns at once if cp->cport is 0. Otherwise it builds an original-direction conntrack tuple with cp's client address and port as source and its virtual address and port (vaddr, vport) as destination, with cp->protocol and cp->af, and looks up the entry in the default zone of cp->ipvs->net with nf_conntrack_find_get. If one is found it calls nf_ct_kill on it (only logging whether it was deleted) and always releases the lookup reference with nf_ct_put; if none is found nothing is taken or released. It takes no reference on cp.
note: Prose matches ip_vs_nfct.c:242-279; the tuple uses the client and virtual address/port pairs, now stated. Slice cut the head (function at 242).

name: start_sync_thread
prose: Function start_sync_thread(ipvs, c, state) starting the IPVS sync daemon threads (state IP_VS_STATE_MASTER or IP_VS_STATE_BACKUP); the packet slice held only part of it (function at ip_vs_sync.c:1763). It returns -ENOPROTOOPT if ip_vs_use_count_inc fails; otherwise it takes the RTNL lock and ipvs->sync_mutex (retrying so as not to hold one while blocking on the other), sets the thread count (from sysctl when no daemon runs yet, else from threads_mask), fills in c's defaults (mcast_af AF_INET and group, port, ttl) and clamps or derives c->sync_maxlen from the interface MTU. Early failures, which go to out_early and only release sync_mutex and the RTNL lock and decrement the module use count (no thread, socket or buffer cleanup, ipvs->ms untouched): -ENODEV if c->mcast_ifn names no device in ipvs->net; -EEXIST if ipvs->ms exists for MASTER or ipvs->backup_tinfo exists for BACKUP; -EINVAL for any other state. For MASTER, ipvs->mcfg (or ipvs->bcfg for BACKUP) is stored before the allocations and stays set even if a later step fails. Later failures (-ENOMEM for the master state array, the thread data array or a backup buffer, the error of make_send_sock or make_receive_sock, or the error of kthread_run) go to out: it releases the RTNL lock, stops the started threads, frees ipvs->ms and sets it NULL only if IP_VS_STATE_MASTER is not set in ipvs->sync_state, releases sync_mutex, releases the sockets and buffers and frees the thread data array, decrements the module use count and returns the error. On success it records the thread data in ipvs->master_tinfo or ipvs->backup_tinfo, sets the state bit in ipvs->sync_state under sync_buff_lock, releases both locks and returns 0, leaving the module use count incremented.
note: Reviewer 15 right: the out_early paths (-ENODEV, -EEXIST, -EINVAL) skip all thread/socket/ms cleanup (ip_vs_sync.c:1947-1953); the old text said every failure did that cleanup. Also noted that the stored mcfg/bcfg are not reverted on later failure.

name: nf_conntrack_expect_init
prose: Function nf_conntrack_expect_init(), called once at module initialization. If nf_ct_expect_hsize is 0 it sets it to nf_conntrack_htable_size / 256, or 1 if that is 0. It sets nf_ct_expect_max = 4 * nf_ct_expect_hsize, creates the expectation slab cache nf_ct_expect_cachep with KMEM_CACHE (returning -ENOMEM if that fails), and allocates the hash table nf_ct_expect_hash with nf_ct_alloc_hashtable(&nf_ct_expect_hsize, 0), which may adjust nf_ct_expect_hsize; if that allocation fails it destroys the cache and returns -ENOMEM. Otherwise it returns 0.
note: Matches nf_conntrack_expect.c:748-767. The old contract was dropped because the function writes several global variables (rule 4).

name: sctp_new_state
prose: Static function sctp_new_state(dir, cur_state, chunk_type) computing the next SCTP conntrack state; dir and cur_state must be valid indexes (IP_CT_DIR_ORIGINAL or IP_CT_DIR_REPLY, and a valid sctp_conntrack value) because they index the table without checking. For chunk_type equal to one of INIT, INIT_ACK, ABORT, SHUTDOWN, SHUTDOWN_ACK, ERROR, COOKIE_ECHO, COOKIE_ACK, SHUTDOWN_COMPLETE, HEARTBEAT or HEARTBEAT_ACK (rows 0 to 10) it returns sctp_conntracks[dir][row][cur_state], which is either a state or SCTP_CONNTRACK_MAX for an invalid transition. For any other chunk type (for example DATA or SACK) it emits a pr_debug message naming cur_state and returns cur_state unchanged. It returns no error code and takes no lock.
note: Prose matches nf_conntrack_proto_sctp.c:188-236; reviewers' points (pr_debug side effect on the default path; table-driven result for known chunk types) are right and stated. No contract because it reads a global table.

name: nf_flow_table_offload_init
prose: Function nf_flow_table_offload_init(). It allocates three unbound workqueues, assigning each to its global: nf_flow_offload_add_wq ("nf_ft_offload_add"), nf_flow_offload_del_wq ("nf_ft_offload_del") and nf_flow_offload_stats_wq ("nf_ft_offload_stats"), each with WQ_UNBOUND | WQ_SYSFS. If the first allocation fails it returns -ENOMEM; if the second fails it destroys the first and returns -ENOMEM; if the third fails it destroys the second and the first and returns -ENOMEM. The globals are not reset after destroy_workqueue (the failing one is NULL from the failed call; the ones destroyed keep dangling pointers). On success it returns 0.
note: Reviewer 15 right: the failing alloc_workqueue stores NULL in its global and the destroyed workqueues' globals are left dangling, not 'unchanged' (nf_flow_table_offload.c:1277-1298). The old contract was dropped because the function writes globals (rule 4).

name: nf_tables_newchain
prose: Static function nf_tables_newchain(skb, info, nla), the nftables NEWCHAIN handler; the commit mutex is held (asserted). It looks the table up (returning its error), then identifies an existing chain: by NFTA_CHAIN_HANDLE (error from nft_chain_lookup_byhandle returned), else by name (an -ENOENT result means the chain is to be created, any other error is returned), and returns -EINVAL if neither handle, name nor NFTA_CHAIN_ID is given. If NFTA_CHAIN_POLICY is present it returns -EOPNOTSUPP when the existing chain is not a base chain or when a new chain has no hook attribute, and -EINVAL for a policy other than NF_DROP or NF_ACCEPT. Flags come from NFTA_CHAIN_FLAGS or the existing chain; flags outside NFT_CHAIN_FLAGS give -EOPNOTSUPP. For an existing chain: -EINVAL if it is a binding chain (NFT_CHAIN_BINDING set on the chain), -EEXIST with NLM_F_EXCL, -EOPNOTSUPP with NLM_F_REPLACE; otherwise it returns nf_tables_updchain(...). For a new chain it returns nf_tables_addchain(...). The return value is therefore 0 or the error from those paths; this function itself does not release anything.
note: Reviewer 15 partly wrong: an existing chain that has the binding flag does return -EINVAL (nf_tables_api.c:3185-3186); binding chains are only allowed on the creation path, via nf_tables_addchain. The old text claimed 'no chain added or modified and all resources released' on every error, which this function cannot guarantee for the helpers' failures. Slice cut the head (function at 3102).

name: nf_tables_newrule
prose: Static function nf_tables_newrule(skb, info, nla), the nftables NEWRULE handler; the commit mutex is held (asserted). It returns the error of nft_table_lookup, then finds the chain by NFTA_RULE_CHAIN or NFTA_RULE_CHAIN_ID (lookup error returned, -EINVAL if neither is given), and returns -EOPNOTSUPP if the chain is bound. With NFTA_RULE_HANDLE the rule must exist (lookup error returned): NLM_F_EXCL gives -EEXIST, NLM_F_REPLACE selects it as old_rule, and without NLM_F_REPLACE it returns -EOPNOTSUPP. Without a handle it returns -EINVAL unless NLM_F_CREATE is set and NLM_F_REPLACE clear, allocates a handle, and resolves NFTA_RULE_POSITION or POSITION_ID to old_rule (lookup error returned). It parses the expressions (up to NFT_RULE_MAXEXPRS = 128, -EINVAL for a non-list-element entry or too many, -ENOMEM if the info array cannot be allocated, or the nf_tables_expr_parse error), returns -EFBIG if the total size reaches 4096, allocates the rule (-ENOMEM), instantiates the expressions (nf_tables_newexpr error returned), creates a flow rule for hardware-offload chains (error returned), increments the chain use count (-EMFILE on overflow), and for NLM_F_REPLACE returns -EOPNOTSUPP for a binding chain, deletes old_rule with nft_delrule (error returned) and inserts the new rule after it; otherwise it queues an NFT_MSG_NEWRULE transaction (-ENOMEM on failure) and links the rule per NLM_F_APPEND and the position. On errors up to this point it unwinds: restores the chain use count, destroys the flow rule and the partly built rule, releases the parsed expression modules and frees expr_info; a successful nft_delrule is not undone if the later transaction allocation fails. On success it frees expr_info, attaches the flow rule to the transaction, and returns the result of nft_table_validate if table->validate_state is NFT_VALIDATE_DO, else 0. A failing nft_table_validate returns its error with the rule already linked and the transaction already queued (no unwinding).
note: Reviewer 15 right: the error from nft_table_validate (nf_tables_api.c:4514-4515) is returned after the rule is linked and the transaction queued, so the old 'rule list unchanged on every error path' claim was wrong. Slice cut the head (function at 4301).

name: nft_ct_expect_obj_eval
prose: Static function nft_ct_expect_obj_eval(obj, regs, pkt), evaluating an nftables ct expectation object; priv holds l3num, l4proto, dport, timeout and size. It gets the conntrack entry of pkt->skb; if there is none, or it is confirmed or a template, it sets regs->verdict.code = NFT_BREAK and returns. It takes the conntrack helper extension, adding one with nf_ct_helper_ext_add(GFP_ATOMIC) if absent, and sets NF_DROP and returns if that fails. If the number of default-class expectations already attached (help->expecting) is at least priv->size it sets NFT_BREAK and returns. If priv->l3num is NFPROTO_INET it uses the connection's own L3 number. It then allocates an expectation (NF_DROP and return if that fails), initializes it for the default class with the reply-direction source and destination addresses of the connection (the inverse tuple), priv->l4proto and the destination port priv->dport, sets its timeout to jiffies + priv->timeout * HZ, and registers it with nf_ct_expect_related; if that fails it sets regs->verdict.code = NF_DROP, otherwise it leaves the verdict unchanged. The allocated expectation's reference is released with nf_ct_expect_put on both outcomes; the early returns before the allocation have nothing to release.
note: Reviewers' points (NFT_BREAK for missing/confirmed/template ct; NF_DROP, not NFT_BREAK, when the helper extension cannot be added) are right and already in the packet text (nft_ct.c:1302-1314). Fixed 'always releases the expectation reference': only on the paths after allocation.

name: nft_fwd_neigh_eval
prose: Static function nft_fwd_neigh_eval(expr, regs, pkt) forwarding the packet with a neighbour lookup; the RCU read lock is relied on for dev_get_by_index_rcu. The verdict starts as NF_STOLEN and is stored in regs->verdict.code at the exit. It sets NFT_BREAK if priv->nfproto is not NFPROTO_IPV4 or NFPROTO_IPV6 or skb->protocol does not match it, and NF_DROP if skb_try_make_writable fails, the IPv4 TTL or IPv6 hop limit is <= 1, dev_get_by_index_rcu finds no device for the output interface, or nf_dev_xmit_recursion() reports recursion (after local_bh_enable). Before looking up the device it decrements the TTL or hop limit (the decrement stays even if a later step drops the packet). Otherwise, with bottom halves disabled, if the skb headroom is smaller than the device's LL_RESERVED_SPACE and the device has header_ops, it calls skb_expand_head; if that fails it returns NULL after freeing the original skb itself, no transmit happens, bottom halves are re-enabled and the verdict stays NF_STOLEN. Otherwise it sets skb->dev, clears the timestamp, increments the xmit recursion count, calls neigh_xmit (which consumes the skb), decrements the count, re-enables bottom halves and the verdict is NF_STOLEN.
note: Reviewers 1, 2 and 15 right in different parts: expand failure leaves NF_STOLEN (nft_fwd_netdev.c:171-174); the original skb is freed by skb_expand_head on failure (skbuff.c:2390-2392, doc 'frees original skb in case of failures'), so the old 'neither freed nor consumed' was wrong. Also the TTL decrement precedes the device lookup.

name: nft_masq_module_exit
prose: Static __exit function nft_masq_module_exit(void). It calls nft_masq_module_exit_ipv6() and nft_masq_module_exit_inet() (each a no-op when the corresponding config is disabled), nft_unregister_expr(&nft_masq_ipv4_type), and nf_nat_masquerade_inet_unregister_notifiers(). It returns nothing. These undo what nft_masq_module_init registered, which includes the masquerade notifiers via nf_nat_masquerade_inet_register_notifiers.
note: Reviewer 15 wrong: the init function does register the inet masquerade notifiers (nft_masq.c:259-265), the slice just did not include it; the unregistration at 276 is correct. Slice cut the head (function at 271).

name: nft_pipapo_avx2_lookup_4b_32
prose: Static function nft_pipapo_avx2_lookup_4b_32(map, fill, f, offset, pkt, first, last), an AVX2 lookup step for one field of an nft pipapo set; the caller must be inside a kernel FPU section with ymm15 zero. It scans each 256-bit block i of the bitmaps from offset up to f->bsize / NFT_PIPAPO_LONGS_PER_M256. For each block it ANDs the lookup buckets for the 32 nibbles of the first 16 bytes of pkt (the high and low nibble of each byte pkt[0] .. pkt[15], each nibble selecting one of 16 buckets). When first is false and the map block is all zero the block is skipped and left unchanged; if the combined bucket result (ANDed with the map block when first is false) is zero it stores zero into the map block. Otherwise it stores that result into the map block and calls nft_pipapo_avx2_refill on it: with last false that call fills the fill bitmap from the mapping table f->mt for each set bit and clears those bits in the map block and returns the mapping target of the first set bit's entry; with last true it neither touches fill nor clears map and returns the rule index of the block's lowest set bit. The function returns -1 if no block matched (including an empty range). With last true it returns the rule index from the last matching block scanned (each match overwrites the result). With last false it returns, for the first matching block, the refill result divided by XSAVE_YMM_SIZE (later blocks do not change it); per the function's comment this is the first long-word index to check next. It allocates nothing.
note: Reviewers right: it uses 32 nibble buckets (nft_set_pipapo_avx2.c:545-553), and the return follows the code: rule index when last (ret = b), refill result / XSAVE_YMM_SIZE for the first matching block when not last (642-647); the source comment calls it the first filled word index.

name: nft_pipapo_avx2_lookup_8b_1
prose: Static function nft_pipapo_avx2_lookup_8b_1(map, fill, f, offset, pkt, first, last), an AVX2 lookup step for one field of an nft pipapo set; the caller must be inside a kernel FPU section with ymm15 zero. It scans each 256-bit block i of the bitmaps from offset up to f->bsize / NFT_PIPAPO_LONGS_PER_M256. For each block it uses the single bucket selected by pkt[0] (one of 256 buckets). When first is false and the map block is all zero the block is skipped and left unchanged; if the combined bucket result (ANDed with the map block when first is false) is zero it stores zero into the map block. Otherwise it stores that result into the map block and calls nft_pipapo_avx2_refill on it: with last false that call fills the fill bitmap from the mapping table f->mt for each set bit and clears those bits in the map block and returns the mapping target of the first set bit's entry; with last true it neither touches fill nor clears map and returns the rule index of the block's lowest set bit. The function returns -1 if no block matched (including an empty range). With last true it returns the rule index from the last matching block scanned (each match overwrites the result). With last false it returns, for the first matching block, the refill result divided by XSAVE_YMM_SIZE (later blocks do not change it); per the function's comment this is the first long-word index to check next. It allocates nothing.
note: Reviewers right: only bucket pkt[0] is used (nft_set_pipapo_avx2.c:688-695); return description aligned with lines 700-705.

name: nft_pipapo_avx2_lookup_8b_2
prose: Static function nft_pipapo_avx2_lookup_8b_2(map, fill, f, offset, pkt, first, last), an AVX2 lookup step for one field of an nft pipapo set; the caller must be inside a kernel FPU section with ymm15 zero. It scans each 256-bit block i of the bitmaps from offset up to f->bsize / NFT_PIPAPO_LONGS_PER_M256. For each block it ANDs the two buckets selected by pkt[0] and pkt[1] (each one of 256 buckets). When first is false and the map block is all zero the block is skipped and left unchanged; if the combined bucket result (ANDed with the map block when first is false) is zero it stores zero into the map block. Otherwise it stores that result into the map block and calls nft_pipapo_avx2_refill on it: with last false that call fills the fill bitmap from the mapping table f->mt for each set bit and clears those bits in the map block and returns the mapping target of the first set bit's entry; with last true it neither touches fill nor clears map and returns the rule index of the block's lowest set bit. The function returns -1 if no block matched (including an empty range). With last true it returns the rule index from the last matching block scanned (each match overwrites the result). With last false it returns, for the first matching block, the refill result divided by XSAVE_YMM_SIZE (later blocks do not change it); per the function's comment this is the first long-word index to check next. It allocates nothing.
note: Reviewers right: buckets for pkt[0] and pkt[1] only (nft_set_pipapo_avx2.c:746-759); return description aligned with lines 765-770.
